headline_draft: Lenny's Podcast: OpenAI's Head of ChatGPT on Why Hand-Built Agent Loops Are a Passing Phase
summary: Tibo Sottiaux, who leads ChatGPT and Codex at OpenAI, appeared on Lenny's Podcast on October 4 (recorded live at DevDay, hours after shipping Dots). He argues that the majority of internet actions will soon be taken by agents, and that products built today must account for models being roughly 10x better within a year. Sottiaux says hand-crafted agent loops and model pickers are transitional; the goal is a system that learns what users want without configuration. OpenAI plans to merge ChatGPT's chat and work modes into a unified experience, eventually putting all Dots functionality into ChatGPT. He also revealed that OpenAI trained a more capable model (GPT-6.1 Astra) and chose not to release it—a deliberate restraint tied to user-base scale.
why_pm: PMs must stop building for interactive chat and start designing for persistent, autonomous agents. The mental model shifts from 'what does the user click?' to 'what does the system learn and do on behalf of the user?' This reframes discovery, error handling, cost controls, and feature prioritization entirely.
key_facts: Tibo Sottiaux, Head of ChatGPT and Codex at OpenAI
Recorded live at DevDay on October 4, 2026
Majority of internet actions will soon be taken by agents, not humans
Hand-built agent loops are a passing phase; goal is learned, adaptive behavior
ChatGPT chat and work modes will eventually merge into one product
OpenAI trained GPT-6.1 Astra but chose not to release it—structural restraint
120 ex-YC founders now work at OpenAI
quotes: I think the majority of actions on the internet will be taken by agents.
Having to set up and fiddle with your loops… I don't think this is the way that it's going to work.
Builders who are not planning for models roughly 10 times better within a year are going to build the wrong thing.

headline_draft: CoreWeave Forge: The AI Production Loop as a Product — Run, Observe, Curate, Improve, Evaluate, Repeat
summary: CoreWeave announced Forge on September 30 (live from Fully Connected 2026), a unified development layer that connects the entire AI improvement lifecycle—training, inference, observability, evaluation, and post-training—in one environment. Forge bundles Weights & Biases Models, OpenPipe post-training expertise, and the marimo notebook project with CoreWeave's own services. CoreWeave ARIA, a coding agent, is now generally available and automatically analyzes experiment and observability data to propose the next iteration with supporting evidence. MasterClass and Canva are already building on Forge.
why_pm: If shipping fast is table stakes, iteration speed compounds advantage. Forge closes the loop between production signals and model improvement—no more handoffs between fragmented tools. PMs using this will discover bugs, validate hypotheses, and deploy fixes 3–5x faster than teams stuck shuffling data between vendors. This is infrastructure as a competitive edge.
key_facts: CoreWeave Forge announced September 30, 2026 at Fully Connected 2026
Unifies training, inference, observability, evaluation, and post-training in one environment
Integrates Weights & Biases Models, OpenPipe, marimo notebooks, CoreWeave services
CoreWeave ARIA (coding agent) now generally available for analyzing experiments
ARIA proposes next experiments with evidence and reasoning
Agent Lens (observability) detects 20% more critical failures at 1/10th the cost of frontier LLMs
quotes: Engineering teams need to understand those gaps, identify the signals that matter, improve the next version and measure whether the change worked under real operating conditions. All of this has to function as a single, connected system.
The more you ship, the faster you improve. That's the virtuous cycle fueling CoreWeave Forge.
